2023_047_m032123bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of March 21, 2023, at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, called to order by President Schmidt at 7:00 p.m. before an audience of approximately 185. The Board approved a consent agenda (23-021), an Early Middle College partnership with Lawrence Technological University (23-022), and adoption of Bridges in Mathematics 2nd edition and Number Corner 3rd edition for Grades K-5, each by a vote of Yes 6, No 0, with Dr. Philippart absent. Non-agenda public comment, capped at one minute per speaker to allow a full hour, went entirely to parents and students urging the Board to keep the honors program.

**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, March 21, 2023, Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. and adjourned it at 9:52 p.m. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary (typist reference GH/jh).

**Attendance**
Present with Mr. Schmidt: Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, and Wilson. Dr. Philippart was absent. Assistant Superintendent Griffor sat in for Superintendent Machesky, who was in Washington, DC, advocating for special education programs. Administrators present: Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Haezebrouck, House, Detmer, Zawislak, Cross, Harris, Melton, and West. Audience of approximately 185.

**Recognitions** (President Schmidt changed the order of the recognition items)
- Student Spotlight: Creative Guild seniors Sophia Keil (Athens) and Sonia Puri (Troy High), introduced by Thomas Butcher; they discussed their podcast productions.
- Schools of Character: Leonard Elementary and Athens High School honored as State Schools of Character; Martell Elementary and Troy High named Emerging Schools of Character. Athens earned its State designation in 2021 during the pandemic. Leonard was one of only 73 schools nationally awarded the honor this year. Ms. Lori Soifer, Director of Schools of Character, presented certificates on behalf of Character.org.
- Mission Moment: Baker Middle School 7th grader Aryan Khedkar won the Oakland Schools' Scripps Regional Spelling Bee on Saturday, March 4th at Oakland University; introduced by Assistant Superintendent DiPilato and Baker Principal Jonathan Cross.
- Mission Moment: Baker teacher Luchi Cacaj recognized; Principal Cross noted Paula Tutman of Channel 4 News returned to do a story on her classroom, part of 6 years of middle school English Language Arts work with Teacher's College at Columbia University.

**Additions & Deletions / Public Communication (Agenda Items)**
None in both cases.

**Actions**

| Item | Motion | Vote |
|---|---|---|
| 23-021 Consent Agenda, items A-E | Moved Hauff, supported Haupt | Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart |
| 23-022 Early Middle College with LTU | Moved Anne, supported Alic | Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart |
| Elementary math adoption | Moved Wilson, supported Anne | Yes 6, No 0, Absent Philippart |

Consent agenda items: Minutes of the February 7, 2023 Board Workshop; Minutes of the February 14, 2023 Board Meeting; Treasurer's Report - January 2023; Furniture Pilot Purchase; and Adult Ed Laptops.

**Curriculum**
- Report: Fielding/Middle School Design Update, by Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent of Secondary Instruction, with student and teacher feedback on likes, dislikes, challenges and wants.
- Early Middle College: a five-year program for students entering Grade 9 combining high school coursework with the first two years of college, culminating in a high school diploma and at least one of the five EMC on-track graduate outcomes at no cost to student or parents; located at Lawrence Technological University.
- Report: Elementary Math, by Natalie Haezebrouck, Director of Teaching & Learning, and Julia Alder, Curriculum & Instruction Specialist for PreK-5 Math, recommending Bridges in Mathematics 2nd edition and Number Corner 3rd edition by The Math Learning Center for Grades K-5, piloted by 90 TSD teachers, for the 2023-2024 school year.

**Business / Student Representatives**
No business items. Reports from Yara Mashal (International Academy-East), Sara Ali (Athens High School), and Nish Palepu (Troy High School). Alexi Papadelis (Troy College and Career High School) was absent; Mr. Schmidt reported TCCHS held a well-attended Career Fair at the Troy Learning Center that day.

**Public Communication (Non-Agenda Items)**
Given the number of requests, each speaker was limited to one minute, allowing a full hour of comment. Every speaker addressed removal of the honors program and supported keeping it as an option for students.

**Other**
President Schmidt updated the Board on Portrait of a Graduate sessions with students. Board comments covered March is Reading Month, Ramadan beginning Thursday, the Troy Times News supplement, Troy High's performance of Curtains, the furniture pilot, and playground design. Ms. Griffor announced the next Board Workshop for April 4th and the regular meeting for April 18th.
2023_047_m032123bdmtg.verbose:
Official minutes of the Troy Board of Education regular meeting held Tuesday, March 21, 2023, at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, and Wilson were present; Dr. Philippart was absent. Assistant Superintendent Griffor was sitting in for Superintendent Machesky, who was in Washington, DC, advocating for special education programs. Administrators present were Birmingham, DiPilato, Griffor, Haezebrouck, House, Detmer, Zawislak, Cross, Harris, Melton, and West. There were approximately 185 members of the audience. The minutes are signed by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, with the typist reference GH/jh.

RECOGNITION. President Schmidt changed the order of the Recognition items on the agenda. The first recognition was the Student Spotlight, in which students from the Creative Guild are recognized for creative achievements in TSD. The Board welcomed two seniors, Sophia Keil from Athens and Sonia Puri from Troy High. Assistant Superintendent Griffor invited Thomas Butcher to share about the students' work; the two students discussed their podcast productions and answered questions from Board members.

The Board then honored Leonard Elementary School and Athens High School for receiving the State School of Character Award, and Martell Elementary and Troy High for being named Emerging Schools of Character. Athens High School had earned the State School of Character designation during the height of the pandemic in 2021, but the district did not have a chance to honor the school at that time because meetings were not being held in person. Leonard was one of only 73 schools across the nation awarded the honor this year, with both Martell and Troy High recognized in 2023 as Emerging Schools. Character.org certifies schools and districts that embed character into all aspects of school life; the framework includes creating a caring school community, giving students opportunities to practice and reflect on their character strengths, and engaging families and communities as partners. Ms. Lori Soifer, Director of Schools of Character, spoke about each school and presented representatives from all four buildings with a certificate.

A Mission Moment recognized Baker Middle School 7th grade student Aryan Khedkar, who won the Oakland Schools' Scripps Regional Spelling Bee on Saturday, March 4th, at Oakland University. Assistant Superintendent DiPilato invited Mr. Jonathan Cross, Principal at Baker Middle School, to introduce Aryan and discuss the achievement; Aryan answered questions from Board members and shared tips on how to win a spelling bee.

A second Mission Moment recognized Baker classroom teacher Luchi Cacaj. Over the last 6 years the TSD middle school English Language Arts team has worked to improve reading and writing opportunities for students through partnerships with Teacher's College at Columbia University, implementing a new curriculum, embracing the workshop model, and forming partnerships within and across schools. Assistant Superintendent DiPilato asked Baker Principal Jonathan Cross to describe the opportunities provided in Mrs. Cacaj's classroom; Mr. Cross shared that Paula Tutman from Channel 4 News was so impressed with the classroom that she returned to do a story on it. Mrs. Cacaj received congratulations from the Board.

ADDITIONS & DELETIONS: None. PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (AGENDA ITEMS): None.

GENERAL - CONSENT AGENDA, item 23-021. It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Troy Board of Education take action to approve items A, B, C, D, and E on the consent agenda: Minutes of the February 7, 2023, Board of Education Workshop; Minutes of the February 14, 2023, Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report - January 2023; Furniture Pilot Purchase; and Adult Ed Laptops. The vote was Yes: 6, No: 0, Absent: Philippart.

PERSONNEL: None.

CURRICULUM. REPORT: Fielding/Middle School Design Update. Christine DiPilato, Assistant Superintendent of Secondary Instruction, shared a brief PowerPoint and provided an update on the Fielding/Middle School Design project, including feedback from students and teachers about likes and dislikes, challenges and wants. She discussed teaching strategies, effective ways to learn, how to support 21st-Century learners, and how to evolve for the new middle schools' futures.

Early Middle College, item 23-022. The Troy School District is seeking to provide broad, rich, and robust course offerings that inspire, are intellectually challenging, and open more opportunities to future learning. The objective of the Early Middle College (EMC) is to offer students entering Grade 9 a five-year program that combines high school coursework with the first two years of college, culminating in attainment of a high school diploma and at least one of the five EMC on-track graduate outcomes, at no cost to the student or parents. The EMC will be located at Lawrence Technological University (LTU) and will utilize the resources of both LTU and TSD for students admitted to the program. It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Mrs. Alic that the Troy Board of Education approve the proposed Early Middle College partnership with Lawrence Technological University, with program elements to be developed beginning in the 2023/2024 school year. The vote was Yes: 6, No: 0, Absent: Philippart.

REPORT: Elementary Math. Natalie Haezebrouck, Director of Teaching & Learning, and Julia Alder, Curriculum & Instruction Specialist for PreK-5 Math, provided a brief report on the new elementary math program proposed to the Board. Bridges in Mathematics 2nd edition and Number Corner 3rd edition, by The Math Learning Center, for Grades K-5, were recommended for adoption. There was discussion among Board members regarding the new math program, which was piloted by 90 TSD teachers. Board members had the opportunity to visit classrooms in elementary buildings to witness the new student learning process and commented on how impressed they were seeing students' enthusiasm, excitement, and joy in doing math. It was moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mrs. Anne that the recommended mathematics materials for the elementary level be approved for the 2023-2024 school year. The vote was Yes: 6, No: 0, Absent: Philippart.

BUSINESS: None.

Reports from Student Representatives to the Board: Yara Mashal, student representative for International Academy-East, reported on events and activities at her school. Sara Ali, student representative for Athens High School, reported on events and activities at Athens. Nish Palepu, student representative for Troy High School, reported on events and activities at his school. Alexi Papadelis, student representative for Troy College and Career High School, was absent, but Mr. Schmidt shared that TCCHS held a Career Fair at the Troy Learning Center that day and that it was very successful and well-attended.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (NON-AGENDA ITEMS). Mr. Schmidt explained the guidelines for public comment and informed the audience that, due to the number of requests submitted to address the Board, each person would have only one minute to speak, which would allow a full hour of public comment. Every speaker addressed the removal of the honors program and supported keeping it as an option for students. Speakers were: Ms. Justine Perakis, TSD parent; Mrs. Bhargavi Kakasani, TSD parent; Mr. John Rollinger, TSD parent; Ms. Nitali Gandhi, TSD parent; Shivani Angadi, sophomore at Troy High School; George Perakis, senior at Troy High School; Ms. Vicki Mu, senior at Troy High School; Ray Zhang, senior at Troy High School; Mr. Yumin Sheng, TSD parent; Hengguang Li, TSD parent; Mr. Anupam Sule, TSD parent; Mrs. Peggy Chinoski, parent of TSD graduates; Jacqui Pursel, TSD parent; Mrs. Stella Kallis, TSD parent; Mr. Ollie Apahidean, TSD parent; Rp. Rocky Raczkowski, TSD parent; Ms. Shanshan Qiu, TSD parent; Ruihua Han, TSD parent; Fabrice Smielianskas, TSD parent; Mr. Bassam Salem, TSD parent; Mrs. Tracy Owens, TSD parent; Mrs. Disha Chablani, TSD parent; Arya Prasad, senior at Troy High School; Mrs. Shilpa Patel, TSD parent; Meaghan Kovacs, TSD parent; Ms. Katherina Mandia, junior at Troy High School; Mr. Krish Gupta, senior at Troy High School; Nikki Snyder, Dexter resident and member of the state board of education; Cynthia Lin, TSD parent; Mrs. Bo Yang, TSD parent; Aksheet Dutta, senior at Troy High School; Mr. Dale Murrish, former TSD parent; Dr. Changgong Zhou, TSD parent; the mother of Boulan Park Middle School student Ethan Wang; Helen Xu, TSD parent; Mr. Steven Sheng, TSD parent; and Weilong Hao, TSD parent.

OTHER - Portrait of a Graduate. Mr. Schmidt provided a brief update on the conversations and information gathering sessions being held with students throughout the district, noting that the common themes students are asking for align with the District's strategic plan and that good components are being gathered for building the portrait of a graduate.

Board Member Comments. Mr. Haupt thanked teachers for organizing events and reading opportunities for March is Reading Month. Mrs. Anne said she attended most of the student sessions for Portrait of a Graduate discussions and was impressed by what students shared; she noted the Board does not take curriculum changes lightly. Mrs. Alic spoke about how each student is met where they are academically to reach their highest potential, and announced that Ramadan starts on Thursday. Mr. Hauff discussed the Troy Times News supplement and his pride in students' leadership roles. Dr. Wilson spoke about changes to the curriculum program and the District's commitment to meeting students where they are; she congratulated Troy High for its recent performance of Curtains and the outstanding support staff winner and nominees. Ms. Griffor discussed the furniture pilot, shared that students have been invited to work with the team designing playgrounds, thanked parents for attending Parent/Teacher Conferences, and announced the next Board Workshop for April 4th and the regular meeting for April 18th. Mr. Schmidt said most students he spoke with would like longer deadlines to go in depth on projects rather than short deadlines, and enjoy experimentation as an exciting way to learn; he also spoke about the consideration given to every curriculum decision.

ADJOURNMENT. The meeting adjourned at 9:52 p.m.
